back: Economic self-sufficiency, the aim of the Four Year Plan so that Germany would not depend on imports in a war.

front: What was the German Labour Front?
back: The organisation under Robert Ley that replaced the free trade unions in May 1933; it could not bargain or strike.
The Labour Front programme of cheap holidays, cruises and leisure to win workers' loyalty.
A system of import controls and barter trade agreements to save foreign currency.

front: When was the Four Year Plan announced and who ran it?
back: October 1936, under Hermann Göring; its aims were autarky and readiness for war.

front: Roughly how many Germans were unemployed in 1932 and 1938?
back: About 5.6 million in 1932 (about six million at the peak) and about 0.4 million in 1938, by the official figures.

front: Why do official unemployment figures overstate Nazi success?
back: They omit Jews and opponents dismissed, women pushed out of work, men in the RAD and army, and prisoners.
The choice between spending on arms and on consumer goods; after 1936 arms took priority.

front: Why did the Nazi economy depend on war?
back: Rearmament and borrowing could not be sustained without conquered resources; autarky had failed.
